text:
nate: Heads up — seeing a ~15-20% p99 latency regression on the gpt-8k-v2 profile after last night's runtime kernel rollout. Traces point to longer batch assembly waiting plus higher KV miss tail. Can someone on call triage?

ying: Yep, I noticed it on the perf dashboard around 02:40 UTC. p50 looks fine, p99 and tail allocation are busted. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/37456 (link for context).

susan: Timeline note: deploy at 02:14 UTC switched kernel to fused-attn-v2 on canary. Could be a startup penalty for small batches or a kernel prewarm regression.

matt: Uploading quick flame snapshot. Key metrics: `batch_wait_ms` doubled on <8-request partitions. KV miss ratio jumped from ~3% -> ~12% for the affected lanes. Attached snippet: `kv_miss_ms` median -> +6ms.

perf-bot: [alert] perf-alert: p99 +17% for model gpt-8k-v2 (us-west-2). Spike start ts ~3745675600.

julie: Hypothesis: admission headroom shifted because admit_window effectively increased after kernel change — runtime waits longer to form batches due to slower per-request prefetch+kernel init on KV misses. That makes the queue admit larger cohorts and increases tail latency.

nate: Quick proposal: rollback canary to fused-attn-v1 and lower global `admit_window_ms` from 8 -> 4 for the canary. Also throttle new requests with a conservative soft-429 when commit > 95% token budget to avoid cascading tails. Thoughts?

ying: Alternative: reduce `token_budget_target` by 10% for high-variance lanes (short requests) and enable async KV prefetch for those lanes. That should reduce batch assembly waits without touching kernel.

matt: Ran a tiny A/B: 30m with `admit_window_ms=4` -> p99 down ~9% but throughput variance rose slightly. `token_budget_target_pct=90` (i.e., -10%) -> p99 down ~12%, KV-miss ratio held steady. So token budget tweak looks most promising.

julie: Plan of action (short window):
1) Canary rollback to fused-attn-v1 (if rollback fast) OR enable `token_budget_target_pct=90` on the canary lanes immediately.
2) Set `admit_window_ms=4` on canary as a secondary mitigation.
3) Enable soft-429 at `soft_429_threshold=0.95` to prevent overload tail when headroom drains.
4) Monitor p50/p90/p99 and KV miss latency for 30m, then roll to prod if stable.

matt: Quick commands: `kubectl set image deploy/runtime runtime=dkr/redwood-runtime:v1-20260316 --namespace=canary`
Config snippet to patch via configmap:
```yaml
admission:
  admit_window_ms: 4
  token_budget_target_pct: 90
  soft_429_threshold: 0.95
```

nate: I'm pinging @eng-oncall to watch alerts and @eng-runtime for rollback readiness. If rollback can't be fast, let's run the token-budget change and soft-429 immediately.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for runtime=v1-20260316 (triggered by nate). Tracking id: cb-374567.

julie: I'll push the config patch now and follow the 30m checklist. If p99 doesn't improve by at least 8% in 30m we revert.

ying: Also flagging a follow-up perf task: instrument kernel startup path to capture first-batch latency separately (pre-KV vs post-KV) so we can tell where the extra ~6ms is coming from.

nate: Perfect. Thanks all — keep updates short here. If anyone sees unexplained drop in throughput, call it out immediately. :thumbsup:
